fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. The kings of the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites and the rest came together to wage war against Joshua and Israel. The list runs from the hill country all the way to the coast. That's six different peoples gathered around one plan, like a whole office actually showing up for the same meeting.

Spies don't show up in this scene, friend. The text says the men of Israel sampled their provisions but did not seek the counsel of the LORD, and then Joshua made a treaty of peace with them (Joshua 9:14-15). Checking the story with scouts isn't mentioned. The Gibeonites do say their own elders told them to go meet Israel (Joshua 9:11), but that's a different trip.

Not a blessing, friend. Joshua calls it a curse, and the job that comes with it has no end date. The Gibeonites will cut wood and carry water for the house of his God (Joshua 9:23). I think this part is heavy, and it's about as far from a blessing as you can get.

Spying isn't what they say, friend. They tell Joshua they were told the LORD commanded Moses to give Israel all the land and wipe out all its inhabitants (Joshua 9:24). That's why they say they feared for their lives. Not a word about spying in their answer.

That's not their story, friend. The reason they give is fear. They say they knew about the command to give Israel the land and wipe out everyone living in it, so they worried for their own lives (Joshua 9:24). Grabbing Israel's land never comes up in what they tell Joshua.
